transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Julian (Redwood SE), Avery (Redwood CSM), Ravi (CTO), Sofia (Head of ML), Tom (Platform Eng), Nadia (Security)

Summary (auto): quick intake to align on GreenStone’s go-live runway for the Q3 pilot. Focus on networking, security artifacts, performance targets, and pilot measurement. Agreed to share artifacts and schedule benchmark window next week.

[00:00] Priya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we know this is a busy week so we'll keep it tight. quick intros?
[00:08] Ravi (GreenStone): hi all, ravi here, CTO — we'll be owning the pilot from our side. Sofia will lead the model integration, tom will handle infra, nadia on security.
[00:18] Priya: perfect, i'll kick off with a short agenda: confirm success criteria, run through network/security checklist, sketch pilot traffic shape, and map next steps.
[00:29] Julian (Redwood SE): hi team — i'll cover runtime specifics, what we recommend for dedicated vs hosted for your workload, and how to run an initial latency baseline.
[00:40] Tom: sounds good — quick note we have strict outbound whitelist on our prod subnet, need to understand peering and egress IPs.
[00:47] Priya: noted. tom and nadia, we'll surface the VPC peering steps and what logs you can expect; julian can call out port lists.

--- Topics: success metrics and scope ---
[06:12] Sofia: on the ML side, our goals are: sub-250ms median token latency for short chat flows, 99.9% availability in a 1-hour window, and no retention of PII. we'll start with 100 RPS spike capacity for 2 hour load tests.
[06:34] Julian: ok for 100 rps burst — for that profile we normally recommend a small Dedicated pool (reserved) to avoid noisy neighbor issues; hosted can work but tail latencies are more variable. also, we can use prefix KV caching for shorter conversations to lower cost and improve median.
[06:52] Ravi: we'd prefer not to commit to reserved capacity initially if possible — budget constraints. can we use hosted with burst config?
[07:00] Julian: yes you can; there's a burst policy that allows temporary capacity with a throttling fallback. tradeoff is cost vs predictability. if predictability is critical for user-facing checkout flow, Dedicated is safer.

[11:05] Nadia: on security: we need KMS integration with our existing HSM, SAML SSO for console access, and an audit trail pushed to our SIEM. what level of audit logs do you expose?
[11:16] Avery (CSM): we can provide token-level cost and latency traces, per-route logs, and exportable audit events; julian, do you want to speak to KMS?
[11:25] Julian: sure — for Private we can integrate with your KMS via customer-managed keys; for Hosted we provide envelope encryption and a managed KMS unless you opt for Bring Your Own Key. audit logs are available via syslog or S3 export. sometimes our auto-transcription will garble a few service names — but the artifacts are there.

[15:40] Tom: about network — does the peering require fixed egress IPs? our security team insists on them for firewall rules.
[15:48] Julian: Dedicated and Private deployments can provide static egress options; hosted generally uses a dynamic egress but we can front through our NAT gateway in some regions. i'll add the exact ip ranges to the runbook. (note: ip list sometimes changes with region rollouts).

[20:01] Priya: on observability, we recommend enabling per-route dashboards and the tracing hook for the pilot. that will let you map model choice to latency and token costs — handy when you're A/B testing quantization profiles.
[20:17] Sofia: can we get model-level cost breakdowns? we need to show finance the delta between 8-bit quantized and fp16 variants.
[20:23] Julian: yes — the console shows token-level cost and you can compare model variants. we'll share a sample cost spreadsheet. quick caveat though: quantization sometimes changes output subtly; we'll want your eval prompts to check quality regression.

--- Discussion: pilot execution plan ---
[28:45] Priya: pilot plan proposal: week 0 (this week) — onboarding docs and SSO; week 1 — sample traffic ingestion and smoke tests; week 2 — benchmark window (2 hours, 100 rps spikes) with Redwood SE running baseline; week 3 — quality evals and rollback/rollout plan; week 4 — decision meeting for production runway. does that align?
[29:02] Ravi: yes generally, can we compress to 3 weeks if artifacts come quick?
[29:08] Priya: possible — depends on how fast we get the prompt set and network approvals.
[29:12] Sofia: i'll try to get the top-50 prompts and token distribution by friday.

[33:20] Nadia: liability question — in the event of suspected data exposure, what's Redwood's incident response SLA and notification window?
[33:29] Avery: we have incident processes and we commit to 1 hour initial acknowledgement for Dedicated enterprise contracts; for hosted the SLA is in the standard TOS but we can include enterprise addendum. we'll share the security pack.

[39:41] Tom: integration question — do you support model pinning per-route and canary rollouts? we need to route checkout traffic to a stable variant.
[39:51] Julian: yes, per-route version pinning is supported and canary percentages are configurable. automatic fallback policies can route to a lighter model if latency spikes.

[43:10] Ravi: procurement timeline — we aim to sign pilot contract by mid-May, procurement needs pricing appendix and optionally a preliminary SoW.
[43:19] Priya: i'll send the pricing appendix and a short SoW draft first thing.

[48:02] Sofia: small nit — our tokenization is a bit nonstandard for product SKUs, will that change your cost estimates much?
[48:12] Julian: tokenization variances matter; please include a sample of SKU text in the corpus so our cost spreadsheet can model it.

[51:30] Priya: quick recap of next steps: priya to send runbook, pricing appendix, and SSO checklist; julian to propose 3 time windows for the benchmark; sofia to send prompt corpus and token distribution; nadia to confirm SOC2 artifacts needed. all to reconvene after the benchmark. anything else?
[51:58] Ravi: thanks all — let's get that draft SoW so procurement can start.
[52:05] Priya: will do, thanks everyone.

End transcript.
